newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-UK's Mirror buying local paper group.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-UK's Mirror buying local paper group.

text.p: Britain's Mirror Group Plc is expanding its local newspaper operations through a 297 million pound ($501 million) agreed bid for Midland Independent Newspapers (MIN) announced on Friday.
Dealers said that Mirror had spent 69.3 million pounds on Friday morning to acquire 33 million MIN shares at 210 pence each, building a stake of over 23 percent.
The deal represents an important step for the national newspaper group which already has a regional presence in Scotland and Northern Ireland and is now driving into the heart of England.
Midland publishes 44 newspaper titles, including dailies The Birmingham Post and Birmingham Evening Mail in England's second city.
"We are confident that the acquisition of MIN will make a positive and significant contribution to Mirror Group's future growth prospects," said Mirror chief executive David Montgomery.
Mirror and MIN have agreed a price of 210 pence per share, around the level which analysts had expected Mirror to have to pay for Britain's sixth largest regional newspaper publisher.
Mirror shares added 7p to 193p on Friday while Midland Independent rose 5.5p to 194p.
Share analysts said the expansion was a logical one and that a strong performance from MIN in the first half of the year made the price seem acceptable.
"Newspapers are what Mirror do well," said Colin Tennant of UBS.
"MIN is doing a bit better trading wise than expected, Mirror says it can cut costs by five million pounds almost immediately and so they can probably make it earning enhancing from 1998," he added.
Mirror Group's flagship tabloid newspaper is Britain's second best selling daily after Rupert Murdoch's Sun. The company also owns popular Scottish titles the Daily Record and Sunday Mail.
It has recently branched out into cable television through its LIVE TV operation but media ownership laws prevent it from playing a major role in the commercial terrestrial television (ITV) sector.

English local newspapers have long been seen as a likely area for Mirror to move into and speculation linking it with Midland, its partner in the Birmingham Live local cable TV channel, has been rife for months. Mirror said the deal should provide real benefits from shared resources, distribution and advertising.

MIN, a management buy-out from U.S. publisher Ralph Ingersoll in 1991, forecast profit before tax and exceptional items of at least 13.2 million pounds in the first half of the year against 8.3 million a year ago.

Chris Oakley, the MIN chief executive whose stake in the company is worth some 4.5 million pounds, will join the Mirror board when the deal goes through. It is subject to regulatory approval and the green light is not expected before October. ($ = 0.592 British Pounds)
